scope: Two isolated headless Chrome controls for reconstructing independent ordinary arrays; no application or decoder changes.
common: Each case copied 16777216 Float64 values in 262144-value chunks and checked every output value, including a negative-zero sentinel. Separate guarded browser processes used the 4 GiB and 25% CPU limits and confirmed owned-process cleanup.

resizable.method: Compared pre-sized ordinary-array reconstruction with growing an array while copying a transferred resizable buffer backwards, shrinking the source after each chunk, and reversing the completed array. A length-tracking typed view was used after structured-clone transfer.
resizable.observation: Both outputs matched all values. Source backing storage fell with each shrink, but the incremental case had a higher total guarded peak. Array growth and process differences were not individually attributed.

diskBacked.method: Compared direct pre-sized reconstruction with copying the Float64 source into an IndexedDB-backed Blob, deleting its database record, detaching the source, and reading Blob slices into a pre-sized array. The disposable database was deleted after the copy.
diskBacked.observation: Both outputs matched all values. The disk-staged case had a higher total guarded peak. Copy timings exclude Blob staging and allocation.

limitations: These are single synthetic browser controls with separate-process variability; they do not profile full ScanForge restores or establish that every incremental or disk-backed design is infeasible.
Neither prototype is integrated. Production restore ownership, resource, native-comparison and milestone gates remain open.
